key_insight: DeepFEAv2 extends transient FEA surrogate modeling beyond structured meshes by using mesh connectivity to jointly predict node- and element-level outputs over time.
engineering_relevance: It can accelerate high-fidelity mechanical simulation by up to three orders of magnitude, enabling near-real-time analysis across structured and unstructured finite element topologies.
method: Uses the FE connectivity matrix to group features by element and form a mesh-guided input sequence.
Employs a new neural architecture to predict node- and element-based outputs jointly across time.
Adds an FEA-informed optimization strategy to regularize predictions.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on structured and unstructured 3D linear elastic datasets plus a pressure-driven aortic valve case, achieving R^2 up to 0.99, normalized error as low as 0.38%, and up to 87.1% lower error than DeepFEA.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate mesh connectivity and careful handling of topology/element-type variation when transferring to new FE settings.
paper_title: DeepFEAv2: Deep Learning for Transient Finite Element Analysis Beyond Structured Meshes
